---
title: Public videos
description: Give a video a public playback ID so anyone with its URL can watch it, with no token.
---

A video plays through its playback IDs. A **signed** ID, the default, plays
only with a token your backend signs. A **public** ID plays for anyone who
has its URL: a marketing video, a trailer, a page with no sign-in. The video
is still encrypted on disk and in transit, but a public ID hands out its key
to every request.

A video can have both: a signed ID for your members and a public one for
everyone else. Revoking one ID leaves the others playing.

## Before you start

- An API key with `assets:write` (the default scopes include it), or the
  `@clipmux/node` client.
- A video, or a file to upload.

## Make a video public

### At upload

Ask for a public ID when you create the upload:

<Tabs items={['Node', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts
// In clipmuxHandler's upload callback
return { passthrough: 'lesson_42', playback_policies: ['public'] }

// Or with the client
const upload = await clipmux.uploads.create({ size, passthrough: 'lesson_42', playback_policies: ['public'] })
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/uploads \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"size": 10485760, "passthrough": "lesson_42", "playback_policies": ["public"]}'
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

`["signed", "public"]` makes one of each, for example a public ID for a
trailer page and a signed one for paying viewers. `POST /v1/assets` takes the
same `playback_policies` when you import a URL. From the command line:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node upload trailer.mp4 --public
CLIPMUX_API_KEY=cmx_… clipmux push --server https://video.example.com --policy public trailer.mp4
```

### On an existing video

Add a public ID to a video that has a signed one, with
`POST /v1/assets/{id}/playback-ids`:

<Tabs items={['Node', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts
const pid = await clipmux.playbackIds.create('ast_…', { policy: 'public' })
// { id: 'pid_…', policy: 'public', playable: true, status: 'active' }
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/assets/ast_…/playback-ids \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"policy": "public"}'
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

`playable` is `false` until the video has finished encoding. A video can
have up to 1000 playback IDs (`409 too_many_playback_ids`).

## Play it

A public ID's URLs start with `/p/` and carry no token:

```txt
https://media.example.com/p/{playback_id}/master.m3u8
https://media.example.com/p/{playback_id}/poster.jpg
https://media.example.com/p/{playback_id}/tracks/{track_id}.vtt
```

The media origin is `base_url` on the video, or from `GET /v1/app`. In your
pages, give `<clipmux-player>` the media origin and the ID, and no token:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@clipmux/player/element'
</script>
<clipmux-player base-url="https://media.example.com" playback-id="pid_…"></clipmux-player>
```

Any HLS player plays the `master.m3u8` URL as it is; see
[Other players and native apps](/docs/build/play/other-players). ClipMux has
no embed page or iframe: you put the player in your own page.

## Caching

Public bytes may sit in shared caches, such as a CDN in front of your media
origin:

| URL | `Cache-Control` |
| --- | --- |
| `master.m3u8` | `no-store`. It's generated on each request. |
| Segments, rendition playlists and init files | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Their paths change when the video is re-encoded. |
| `poster.jpg` | `public, max-age=300` |
| `tracks/{track_id}.vtt` | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| `key/…` (the content key) | `no-store` |

Signed IDs send `private` instead of `public`, so their bytes stay out of
shared caches.

## Stop a public video

Revoke the public ID, and its URLs stop working. The video's other IDs keep
playing:

```ts
await clipmux.playbackIds.delete('ast_…', 'pid_…')
```

`DELETE /v1/assets/{id}/playback-ids/{pid}` answers `202 revoking` while the
ID is unpublished and `200 revoked` once it is gone. The master playlist is
never cached, so a revoked ID can't start playing again.

## Free previews: a signed ID with an open token

To let anyone watch for a while, such as a free lesson, you don't need a
public ID. Keep the signed ID, and have your backend sign a token for every
visitor without an access check. You can stop it at any time in your own
code, and a URL someone copies dies with its token. A public ID's URL
works until you revoke the ID.

## Check it works

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://media.example.com/p/pid_…/master.m3u8
```

- `200`: the ID is public and the video is ready.
- `403 denied`: the ID is signed. Use a `/v/{token}/…` URL, or add a public
  ID.
- `404`: the ID was revoked or doesn't exist, or the video isn't ready yet.
